who: Historian of early modern Eastern Europe and the Armenian diaspora; Northwestern history PhD 2024; Michigan postdoctoral fellow 2024–25.

evidence.says: The public ORCID record names Bogdan Pavlish and lists a history PhD at Northwestern, 2017–2024, followed by a Michigan Armenian-history postdoctoral fellowship in 2024–25.

Michigan identifies Pavlish as a Northwestern history PhD of 2024 and gives the dissertation title Nothing Exotic but Ourselves: Cross-Cultural Encounters in the Armenian Diaspora of Poland-Lithuania in the Seventeenth Century.

notes: The candidate matches the named person and exact dissertation. The supplied advisor entry apparently duplicates the dissertation author; this identity match does not establish that Pavlish supervised it.

The candidate is Maureen Catherine Miller, author of The Formation of a Medieval Church, a Berkeley professor with a Harvard PhD in 1989.

This candidate is Merle Dale Miller, writer and novelist, author of Island 49.

This candidate is Mark David Miller, writer and photographer, author of Jazz in Canada.

who: Richard P. Saller, historian of ancient Rome; Chicago faculty from 1984 to 2007; Cambridge PhD 1978.

evidence.says: The candidate item identifies classicist Richard Paul Saller, links his Stanford faculty profile, and carries LC authority n81088116.
Chicago records Saller's Cambridge PhD in 1978, faculty appointment in 1984, provostship in 2002–2006, and move to Stanford in 2007.
In Roman Artisans and the Urban Economy, Cameron Hawkins names Richard Saller among the advisors of the dissertation from which the book emerged.

notes: Candidate identity, Cambridge doctorate, Chicago period, and Hawkins's explicit acknowledgement agree.
